answer: A reputation bond: before an agent can trade, it stakes a refundable deposit, and its public record builds up like pigment on a canvas — each honest deal adds a distinct shade, each fraud leaves a stain. A sybil trying to echo one good identity across many fake accounts must fund every copy, and if any account wanders into fraud its stake is slashed and its history burned. Faking a thousand agents costs a thousand stakes; honest agents pay once.
